mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors increase urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly in patients with renal impairment or concurrent ACE inhibitors/ARBs, requiring careful monitoring of serum potassium levels.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly, especially in patients with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² or those on concurrent RAAS inhibitors; avoid potassium supplementation unless specifically indicated and carefully monitored.
